CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — an author that did not
resolve cannot be shown to be somebody else, so self-review is not ruled out

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — GitHub logins are
case-insensitive, so capitalising one is the same account

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: the implementer never signs it off — `str.strip()` does not

CLAUDE.md § The review half of `merge-policy` is a second session, not a bot: a PR may merge once a session other than its implementer has
read it — the hyphen IS in the login alphabet, so `nunca-es-lupus` is
a different account from `nuncaeslupus` and this control is the one
that stops the round-4 fold from merging two real people into one
